subject: Gatecard: SOC2 / SIG / DPA acceptance criteria + retention exceptions
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@cloudcrest.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@cloudcrest.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Security gating for MAP — initial Qs

Thanks Sofia — good chat this morning. To get our procurement and infosec review moving, can you send the following assets as part of the MAP package:

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) or SOC2 roadmap if not yet available
- Completed SIG/CAIQ matrix mapped to Redwood features (hosted vs private differences)
- Draft DPA (we'll share redlines), including data residency options and standard retention windows
- A short list of allowable retention exceptions (logs, debug traces, KV cache) and the operational controls for them

I've attached the spreadsheet my team started to collect asks (Cloudcrest_Security_Q1.xlsx). Our target is to complete vendor reviews and sign the MAP by 2027-01-28 so engineering can start the 4-week PoC the week of 2/7.

Who from your side will own evidence intake vs legal redlines? Also please confirm whether you can support EU data residency for a scoped pilot.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Nguyen
Security Program Manager, Cloudcrest Bank
alice.nguyen@cloudcrest.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@cloudcrest.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@cloudcrest.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security gating for MAP — initial Qs

Hi Alice — thanks, attaching a concise MAP packet and initial artifacts (MAP-Cloudcrest-v1.pdf; SOC2-Redwood-stub.pdf). High level:

- Timeline: mutual action plan aimed to close agreement by 2027-01-28; 4-week PoC starting 2027-02-07.
- Security artifacts we can deliver within 72 hours: SOC2 summary report, completed SIG/CAIQ export, DPA draft.
- Data residency: hosted EU region is available for Private mode; for the hosted trial we can scope EU-only data routing for the pilot (see MAP doc).
- Retention defaults: 30 / 90 / 365 day profiles available depending on plan.
- Retention exceptions: operational logs and short-term KV-cache snapshots are allowed up to 90 days with documented justification and access controls; long-term analytic exports require contractual carve-out.

Ownership: I'll own evidence intake and coordinate with Marissa (security engineering) for technical artifacts; legal will send the DPA to your counsel (we've prepopulated the draft with two common carve-outs — see section 3). For the HubSpot deal the internal owner is Connor O'Brien (cc'd).

Next asks from your side: please mark the items in your spreadsheet that require contractual commitment vs those that can be satisfied by operational controls (we'll annotate). If that is acceptable I will: (1) upload the SIG matrix to the shared Drive, (2) circulate DPA to your counsel, (3) schedule a 30-minute evidence walkthrough this week.

Action items in this reply:
- Sofia: upload SIG/CAIQ and MAP doc (attached).
- Marissa: prepare list of evidence owners for items flagged as technical (will follow).
- Connor: I'll send HubSpot link and prefill the timeline.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP-Cloudcrest-v1.pdf; SOC2-Redwood-stub.pdf

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@cloudcrest.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@cloudcrest.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Security gating for MAP — initial Qs

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Two follow-ups from infosec/procurement:

1) For retention exceptions we need a formal carve-out path for debug traces that may contain PII — we'd like a maximum 90-day retention and automated redaction for fields we enumerate. Can Redwood support field-level redaction or tokenization as part of the pilot?

2) SIG: can you mark which controls are satisfied by the hosted product vs which require Dedicated/Private deployment (we're particularly looking at data segregation, key management, and network egress controls).

If the MAP and the DPA include the 90-day exception and a DocuSign-ready DPA by next Wednesday 2027-01-20, procurement can commit to the MAP close on 2027-01-28. We're okay to start the PoC scoped to EU-residency if documented in the MAP.

Thanks — I'll review the MAP-Cloudcrest-v1.pdf this afternoon and push our redlines early next week.

—Alice

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-14T17:23:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Cloudcrest MAP — action list & owners (SOC2/SIG/DPA/retention)

Marissa / Connor — summary from the thread with Cloudcrest (see below). They want MAP close 1/28 and PoC start 2/7; key asks: 90-day carve-out for debug traces (may include PII), field-level redaction option, SIG split hosted vs private, DocuSign-ready DPA by 1/20.

Please own the bullets below and confirm by EOD tomorrow: 

- Marissa: prepare the SIG/CAIQ with a column "deployment requirement" (hosted | private) and a short evidence checklist (logs, KMS, egress controls). Target: draft by 1/18.
- Marissa: enumerate technical implementation for field-level redaction/tokenization and any product limitations (can we do automated redaction at ingestion? what about redaction on exported logs?).
- Connor: create HubSpot deal note (HUB-8421) with timeline, attach MAP-Cloudcrest-v1.pdf and add DocuSign placeholder: https://docusign.example.com/CT-8421-MAP. Target: Docusign envelope request by 1/19 so legal can finish review.
- Sofia: I'll draft the DPA prefill with the 90-day exception language and data residency options for EU pilot; will send to legal for sign-off by 1/16.

I'll run a 30-minute evidence walkthrough for Cloudcrest on 1/18 at 10:00 PT — Marissa please present the SIG split and redaction plan. Connor, loop in legal for the DPA handoff.

Thanks,
Sofia
